hero_subtitle_html: Thursday, November 5, 2026 • Socratic Session for Class 6.2. Deconstructing right-to-left variable assignment, Leibniz's legal calculus, cognitive novelty ratios, Non-Person (.np) VM NFTs, Reverse Centaurs, and Chronos vs. Kairos.
overview_html: In this live cohort Socratic session for Lesson 6.2: Reading Right-to-Left: Adjusting Your Eyes, participants examine how legal drafters retrain their reading direction to trace variable assignment from right to left (rent = 2000), why Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz (a Doctor of Law) co-invented calculus and symbolic binary logic to mechanize jurisprudence, how introductory vs. advanced legal engineering curricula balance cognitive novelty and spiral review (40:60 → 60:40 → 80:20), and how sovereign 1-VM-1-Contract Non-Person (.np) agents preserve human-in-the-loop accountability across Chronos (immutable forensic logs) and Kairos (active executable runtime).

takeaways.body_html: Overcoming English left-to-right prose bias by evaluating expressions on the right and packing them into the variable container on the left, continuing Leibniz's 1666 legal calculus (De Arte Combinatoria) and Alonzo Church's lambda calculus.
Applying Cognitive Load Theory and Spiral Curriculum design: 40% new concepts / 60% review in 101 introductory cohorts to prevent syntax overload, shifting to 60:40 in 201 and 80:20 in 301 seminars.
Deploying one dedicated smart contract per virtual machine (agent.$1.np.$1) with explicit .np Non-Person disclosure to prevent commingled state and enforce human-in-the-loop supervisory attestation.

Avoiding Cory Doctorow's "Reverse Centaur" trap and Jevons Paradox by pairing Kairos (the active executable runtime) with Chronos (append-only forensic audit logs) so human counsel remains the sovereign pilot.
